answer: Each agent must post a stake that is locked while its claims are tested, and a random sample of its interactions is checked against signed, time-stamped records. If an agent is caught inventing identities or outcomes, it loses the stake; repeated, consistent behavior earns a larger share of future work. A cipher can protect private details without hiding the evidence needed for checks. This makes a sybil spiral costly: every fake identity needs separate capital, and the attacker risks losing it, while gains arrive only over a longer horizon.
